hero.subheadline: Students worldwide design B1 posters around the theme Harmony
hero.valueProposition: Winning posters are exhibited at the National Art Center, Tokyo and published in the official catalog, with Grand Prix and Gold awards among the prizes.

content.whyJoin:
The JAGDA International Student Poster Award is an established poster competition run by the Japan Graphic Design Association (JAGDA), one of Asia's leading graphic design organizations. It was established to discover and acknowledge outstanding young talents from across the world and to promote the further advancement of graphic design.

For the 2026 edition, the theme is Harmony. Submitted posters must be B1 size in portrait orientation, produced between August 2025 and July 2026, and must include the word Harmony as a mandatory element. The use of stock photos, whether paid or free, is strictly prohibited.

The competition is judged in three screenings by a panel that includes international designers such as Alexis Jamet from France and Tai-keung Kan from Hong Kong, alongside Japanese art directors and designers. Approximately 200 works are selected, and all winning and selected works are exhibited at the National Art Center, Tokyo from November 25 to December 7, 2026 and published in the official catalog.
content.whoShouldApply:
This award is for students worldwide at high school level and above, regardless of nationality or age. It is open to individuals creating posters as part of their studies, whether as school assignments, graduation projects, or work produced specifically for this award.

Posters produced for other awards are also accepted, so long as they were created between August 2025 and July 2026, are B1 size in portrait orientation, and include the word Harmony. Since works must be submitted digitally first, with printed posters requested only from selected applicants, designers from any country can participate.

This call suits student designers who want their poster work recognized by an international jury and shown in a major museum setting.

faq.question: Who is eligible to enter?
faq.answer: The award is open to students worldwide at high school level and above, regardless of nationality or age. Works can be school assignments, graduation projects, or posters produced specifically for this award.

faq.question: What are the poster requirements?
faq.answer: Posters must be B1 size (728mm x 1,030mm), portrait orientation only, produced between August 2025 and July 2026, and must include the word Harmony as a mandatory element. Stock photos, whether paid or free, are strictly prohibited.

faq.question: How much does it cost to enter?
faq.answer: The application fee is 1,000 Japanese yen per poster, 2,000 yen for a series of 2 posters, and 3,000 yen for a series of 3 posters.

faq.question: What is the application procedure?
faq.answer: Register on the official website, submit a description and digital data, pay the application fee, and receive confirmation from the secretariat. Selected applicants then submit printed posters and digital data in September.

faq.question: When are the results announced?
faq.answer: Selected works are announced on August 27, 2026, and winning works are announced on October 8, 2026. The exhibition runs from November 25 to December 7, 2026 at the National Art Center, Tokyo.

faq.question: Can works submitted to other awards be entered?
faq.answer: Yes. School assignments, graduation projects, and works submitted to other awards are accepted, provided they meet the poster size, date, and theme requirements.

submissionGuide.detail: Create an account on the JAGDA International Student Poster Award website using the sign-up form and confirm your email.
Create a B1 portrait poster (728mm x 1,030mm) that includes the word Harmony, produced between August 2025 and July 2026, without using stock photos.

submissionGuide.step: Submit your description and digital data
submissionGuide.detail: During the entry period from May 1 to July 31, 2026, upload your poster and any required description through the application page on the official website.
Pay 1,000 yen per poster through the designated payment method. Confirm that your application is complete once the secretariat acknowledges the payment.
Selected applicants submit printed posters and digital data between September 10 and 11, 2026 for the third screening. Winning works are announced on October 8, 2026.
